chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mudabbir (a slave manumitted upon the master's death), so he said: 'He is in the position of the will (wasiyyah); he returns (to full freedom) in whatever he chooses from it.'

key_terms.المُدَبَّر: Mudabbir: A slave manumitted upon the master's death, who must pay his value from the estate.
key_terms.الوَصِيَّة: Al-Wasiyyah: The one-third of the estate bequeathed to a non-heir, used here as a legal analogy for the Mudabbir's debt.
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: Yarji'u: He returns or reverts (to freedom) by paying off the debt.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a Mudabbir slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the *Mudabbir* (a slave promised freedom upon the master's death) holds a legal status equivalent to the *Wasiyyah* (the one-third bequest), allowing him to select specific assets from the estate to settle his manumission debt. This ruling underscores the priority of the *Mudabbir*'s freedom over general heirs, reflecting the Shia juristic view that his emancipation is a debt owed by the estate, similar to a bequest, rather than a gift. The narration highlights the flexibility in asset selection, ensuring the slave can secure his freedom without being restricted to a fixed portion of the inheritance.
